style.vernacular: A long thin Georgian-era town in a steep dry valley: 2-3 storey lime-washed or painted-render terraces along Main Street with sash windows, fanlights and small balconies, built partly of local volcanic stone; white-and-cream government buildings and East India Company fortifications at the harbour end; most roofs now grey or red metal sheet (formerly slate); barren dark cliffs above with sparse palms and shade trees.
style.ornament: Georgian sash windows with white-painted glazing bars, fanlights over doors, shallow pediments and quoins, iron balcony rails, crenellated and bastioned East India Company walls with cannon, Napoleonic-era heritage plaques.

sources.what: long thin town in James Valley, many buildings of local volcanic rock, over 100 listed Georgian buildings, Main Street unspoilt Georgian; Jacob's Ladder; St James' Church
The Castle: white buildings, not like a typical castle, upper storey added 1776, rebuilt 1860s
roof originally slate, now metal sheeting as on most buildings on the island
